reviewer: native_acceptance independent source and focused execution review
status: Accepted for the bounded QA-only diagnostic purpose; no source blocker found.

reviewedIntegration.boundary: Source review of snapshot/collection placement and original exit preservation only; the separate host renderer candidate has another independent review.

identityReview: Requires Linux, CI=true, QA environment, numeric current run/PID and a launch timestamp no older than two hours.
The snapshot runs after emulator boot/app installation and before Maestro, so the captured executable is past the normal launcher-to-QEMU transition.

Reads fixed proc stat/status/exe and boot_id inputs only. Checks UID, live state, executable canonical path within the SDK allowlist, regular/executable inode identity and unchanged start ticks/executable across reads.

Collection validates the saved run/PID/launch/boot identity and snapshot timing. If the PID still exists, it rejects UID/start-tick/executable changes or a racing reuse; a departed process is an expected diagnostic case.
Saved JSON reads reject duplicate keys, symlinks, hardlinks, owner mismatch, oversize and observed file mutation. Output files are exclusively created through the owned, non-symlink log directory.

journalReview.query: One fixed noninteractive sudo command executes /usr/bin/timeout and /usr/bin/journalctl. No shell, dynamic command, coredump extraction, retry or privilege escalation beyond the approved journal read is exposed.
journalReview.selection: Exact coredump MESSAGE_ID, boot, crashed-process PID/UID/executable and current-run crash interval are selected and revalidated. The helper deliberately does not confuse coredump process fields with the journal emitter PID/UID.
journalReview.privacy: Only explicit metadata/message fields survive reconstruction. No raw stderr, environment, command-line, maps, process memory or core bytes are retained; query failure records an allowlisted reason and counts.
journalReview.failureStates: Absent/unsupported/denied/timed-out queries remain unavailable; output limits or rejected records are partial; multiple matching crash records are ambiguous. These states cannot pass an app gate.

processAndExitReview: The privileged command has its own absolute-path GNU timeout, so terminating the nonprivileged observer does not require permission to kill a root child to establish its intended query bound.
The controlled subprocess reader drains both pipes independently and records overflow/timeout, then terminates/kills and waits for the child. Raw output is discarded after parsing/selecting fields.
The runner saves the incoming gate status before cleanup, calls both diagnostics as best effort, and exits with that saved status. Existing flow/evidence/decoder verdicts remain authoritative.
The helper is included in the preparation source list, disposable preparation test fixture and existing native-ui workflow path glob. No review edit was made to these paths.

verification.environmentChange: NODE_TEST_CONTEXT omitted for this standalone focused run

limits: The 47 tests use synthetic proc/journal fixtures and real controlled ordinary subprocesses. No local sudo query, systemd-coredump capture, real emulator core processing or current native CI execution was performed for this review.
Journal coredump fields do not contain a start-tick equality proof. They correlate a saved identity and bounded interval; the receipt correctly retains this limitation.

The query runs after emulator cleanup. A later matching record cannot on its own establish that the crash caused an earlier UI failure; timestamps and the original gate result must be assessed together.
Existing journal availability, permissions and asynchronous crash-summary timing are unknown until the next CI run. No matching saved record does not imply there was no crash.
This diagnostic does not change or prove the proposed Mesa renderer isolation, fix the observed b5 SIGSEGV, or establish full native navigation/capture/movie acceptance.
